# Fixture 0076 — access-log `status_code_filter` (`GE 500`, byte-exact)

The **FIRST access-log FILTER witness** (phase 70, ADR-0140 / ADR-0141). Every
prior access-log fixture (0012 / 0040 / 0046-0070) carries an UNFILTERED sink,
where every record reaches the file. This fixture witnesses the per-record
emission PREDICATE: an `AccessLog` entry carrying
`filter.status_code_filter.comparison { op: GE, value.default_value: 500 }`
emits the 503 record and DROPS the 200 — byte-exact cross-proxy.

## What this proves (the filter decision is cross-proxy identical on BOTH halves)

One HCM listener, one file sink, two `direct_response` routes probed once each:

| # | request      | response | comparison (`GE 500`) | emitted? |
|---|--------------|----------|-----------------------|----------|
| 1 | `GET /log`   | 503      | `503 >= 500` → match  | YES      |
| 2 | `GET /nolog` | 200      | `200 >= 500` → miss   | NO       |

So each proxy's file holds EXACTLY ONE line (measured against the pinned
`envoyproxy/envoy:v1.33.0`):

```
STATUS=503 PATH=/log FLAGS=-
```

Both halves are load-bearing. The KEPT half proves the filter does not suppress
a matching record; the DROPPED half proves it suppresses a non-matching one. A
one-sided disagreement — either proxy emitting a `/nolog` line, or either proxy
dropping the `/log` line — fails the driver's line-count assertion before the
byte compare is even reached. Passing therefore requires both proxies to agree
on the decision AND on the rendered bytes.

`%RESPONSE_FLAGS%` renders the no-flags sentinel `-` even on the 503: a
`direct_response` is generated by the HCM itself, so no upstream failure flag
applies (state-1 recon, ADR-0140 — a `direct_response` 503 carries
`%RESPONSE_FLAGS%` = `-`). The status is DIRECT_RESPONSE-authored rather than
upstream-derived, which is what keeps the fixture deterministic.

The assertion is **pure cross-proxy equality** — there is NO static expected
literal. The line above is documentation of the measured value, not the oracle.

## `runtime_key` is mandatory but inert

`value.runtime_key: unused` is present because upstream PGV marks it
`min_len 1`; envoy-rust rejects an empty one
(`ConfigError::EmptyStatusCodeFilterRuntimeKey`). It is RTDS-inert on both
sides — there is no runtime subsystem, so the comparison always reads
`default_value`. Its literal value never reaches the wire or the log.

## Probes / driver

`kind: http1_access_log_byte_exact` — drives the probe sequence, scrapes both
files, asserts the scraped line count equals `expected_logged_count(probes)`,
and calls `access_log::assert_access_log_lines_byte_identical`. Probe 2 carries
`expect_logged: false` (phase 70, ADR-0141), which excludes it from that count;
without it the flush poll would wait for a second line that neither proxy will
ever write, and burn the full `ACCESS_LOG_FLUSH_WAIT`. The field defaults to
`true`, so all pre-existing byte-exact fixtures are untouched.

`clusters: []` — both routes are `direct_response`, so there is no upstream: no
backend spawns and no `{{BACKEND_IP}}` / `{{HTTP1_BACKEND_PORT}}` machinery is
needed (the 0040 / 0050 / 0056 `direct_response` template shape).

## Per-side divergences

| Side       | bind address | admin block  | access-log path                         | `generate_request_id`   |
|------------|--------------|--------------|-----------------------------------------|-------------------------|
| envoy      | `0.0.0.0`    | yes (port 0) | `/tmp/0076-envoy-mount/access.log`      | `false` (load-bearing)  |
| envoy-rust | `127.0.0.1`  | omitted      | `/tmp/0076-envoy-rust-mount/access.log` | omitted (never injects) |

The route table, the `text_format_source`, and the `filter` block are
BYTE-IDENTICAL across the two files — only the four documented per-side deltas
above differ, exactly as in fixtures 0040 / 0056. The parent directory is
bind-mounted from the host into the Envoy container so the harness can read the
access.log file after the requests complete.

## Cross-references

- ADR: ADR-0140 (state-1 brainstorm — the `status_code_filter` pick as the
  accesslog FILTER subsystem opener; the measured `direct_response`-is-logged /
  `FLAGS=-` recon), ADR-0141 (state-2 PLAN — the config schema, the
  `should_log(final_response_code)` sink gate on both the H1 and H2 emit loops,
  and the `expect_logged` driver extension).
- Related fixtures: 0040 (the `text_format_source` command-operator template
  this is shaped after), 0050 / 0056 (the `direct_response` access-log
  template), 0012 / 0046 (the happy-path `%RESPONSE_FLAGS%` = `-` baselines).
- Deferred: the H2 sibling of this filter witness (the sink gate IS wired into
  the H2 emit loop and the `expect_logged` extension IS mirrored into the H2
  byte-exact arm, but no H2 fixture exercises a suppressed probe yet); the `EQ`
  / `LE` comparison ops (schema-supported, unit-tested, no differential
  witness); the RTDS `runtime_key` override path (no runtime subsystem).
